answer: PoA binds each identity to slashed collateral: every agent stakes a bond to open a voyage into the agent economy, and its reputation accumulates like a river whose flow is measured by independent peer attestations of distinct, verifiable work. Forking many fake identities to game the river is costly because each Sybil still needs its own bond plus ongoing compute, and if peers flag duplicates the stake is slashed. A coordinated Sybil army can only operate at its nadir — where the marginal cost of a new bond and the slashed-loss risk exceed the reward one diluted identity can extract.
